title: How to Make Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes with Five‑Blade Scissors

meta_description: Learn how to make herb‑infused butter cubes using five‑blade scissors for fast, fragrant results. Follow step‑by‑step tips and get the most out of your Herb Sci
html:
Herb‑infused butter cubes are a game‑changer for quick flavor boosts, and using a pair of five‑blade scissors makes the process faster and more consistent. In this guide, we’ll walk through chopping fresh herbs, blending them into butter, and freezing the mixture into handy cubes—perfect for sautéing, spreading, or tossing into pasta. The key tool? Herb Scissors: five‑blade herb shears that mince cilantro, chives, and basil in one snip, complete with a cleaning comb.

Why Use Five‑Blade Scissors for Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes

Traditional chopping knives can produce uneven pieces, leading to pockets of herb‑free butter and a less uniform flavor. The five‑blade design of the Herb Scissors cuts herbs into fine, consistent shreds with a single motion. This means:

  • Even distribution of herb particles throughout the butter
  • Reduced prep time—no need to dice, then mince
  • Less mess on the cutting board; the herbs stay contained in the scissor’s bowl

Because the blades are staggered, they also create a gentle crush that releases essential oils without bruising the leaves, preserving their bright color and aroma.

Choosing the Right Herbs and Butter

For herb infused butter cubes, freshness is everything. Pick herbs that are vibrant, free of wilting, and have been washed and patted dry. Common combos include:

  • Parsley, chives, and lemon zest for a classic finishing butter
  • Basil, cilantro, and minced garlic for an Italian‑Mediterranean twist
  • Thyme, rosemary, and smoked paprika for a robust, grill‑ready cube

Use high‑quality unsalted butter—preferably European‑style for its higher butterfat content, which yields a richer mouthfeel and holds herb flavor longer. Soften the butter to a spreadable consistency before mixing; this prevents clumping and makes it easier to incorporate the minced herbs.

Step‑by‑Step: Making Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes with Five‑Blade Scissors

  1. Prep the herbs. Remove any tough stems, gather a handful of leaves, and place them in the bowl of the Herb Scissors.
  2. Snip and mince. Close the scissors firmly and pull the handles together. The five blades will shred the herbs into fine pieces in one motion. For larger batches, repeat until you have the desired amount.
  3. Combine with butter. Transfer the minced herbs to a mixing bowl containing softened butter. Add a pinch of salt and any optional flavorings (lemon zest, crushed pepper, etc.).
  4. Blend thoroughly. Use a spatula or wooden spoon to fold the herbs into the butter, ensuring an even distribution. The finer the herb cut, the more uniform the flavor.
  5. Portion and freeze. Spoon the mixture onto a sheet of parchment paper and roll into a log, or use silicone ice‑cube trays for individual cubes. Cover and freeze for at least two hours.
  6. Store for future use. Once solid, pop the butter cubes out of the tray and transfer them to an airtight container or zip‑top bag. They’ll keep in the freezer for up to three months.

When you need a burst of herb flavor, simply drop a cube into a hot pan, melt it over steamed vegetables, or crumble it onto grilled fish. The five‑blade scissors have already done the heavy lifting, so you get consistent results every time.

Tips for Perfecting Your Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes

Even with the best tools, a few tricks can elevate the final product:

  • Dry herbs completely. Any remaining water will turn the butter grainy when frozen.
  • Don’t over‑soften the butter. It should be pliable, not melted, to avoid separating the butterfat and water.
  • Use the cleaning comb. After each batch, pull the comb through the scissor blades to remove stuck herb fibers. This keeps the Herb Scissors performing at peak efficiency.
  • Adjust herb ratios. Start with a 1:4 herb‑to‑butter ratio (e.g., ¼ cup herbs to 1 cup butter) and tweak to taste.
  • Freeze on parchment. This prevents the butter from sticking and makes it easier to transfer to storage containers.

Creative Uses for Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes

Once you have a stash of herb infused butter cubes, the culinary possibilities expand:

  • Steak finishing butter. Drop a rosemary‑garlic cube onto a hot steak for an instant sauce.
  • Pasta boost. Toss a basil‑citrus cube into hot pasta; the butter melts, coating noodles with aromatic oil.
  • Breakfast upgrades. Melt a chive‑cheddar cube over scrambled eggs for a cheesy herb note.
  • Grilled veg. Slide a cumin‑lime cube onto corn or zucchini on the grill for a quick glaze.

The convenience of pre‑portioned cubes means you can add flavor without measuring or chopping at the last minute, keeping your kitchen workflow smooth.

FAQ

Can I use frozen herb‑infused butter cubes directly from the freezer?

Yes. The cubes are designed to melt quickly when added to a hot pan or dish. Just drop them in, and the butter will release the herbs as it thaws.

Do the five‑blade scissors work with tougher herbs like rosemary?

They handle soft to medium‑tough herbs best. For very woody stems, strip the leaves first or give them a quick chop with a knife before using the Herb Scissors.

Is the cleaning comb necessary after each use?

While not strictly required, using the comb keeps the blades free of dried herb fragments, preserving the scissors’ cutting efficiency and preventing cross‑contamination between different herbs.
